new.headline: Week one was clean, so next week keeps the same three walk-run days and adds a single extra minute of running on Saturday, only if the shin stays quiet. The check the morning after each run decides every step.

flags.title: Morning-after check
flags.detail: Each run needs pain at 0/10 and a quiet shin the next morning. Sunday morning, after Saturday's run, decides whether next week steps up or repeats.

flags.title: Stop rule
flags.detail: If the shin aches during a run, stop and walk. Pain above 3/10, or worse the next morning, means we shorten the next session. Tell your physio if it happens.

flags.title: Goal date
flags.detail: A 30-minute continuous run by mid-October is too soon for a safe build. I would move it to around the turn of the year.

flags.title: Feeling good
flags.detail: You rated Saturday 9/10 for how you felt. Hold effort at about 3/10 and the same walking pace between runs, because your fitness will come back faster than your shin.

new.analysis:
Week one was a clean start. You did three walk-run sessions, pain was 0/10 on every run, your shin was quiet afterwards, and heart rate stayed in zones 1 and 2. That counts as the first pain-free week of the four in a row you need.

The 45 minutes in your weekly report is time on the move, including walking. Your splits read as five rounds of 1 minute running and 2 minutes walking per session, so you ran about 15 minutes in total. If you did it differently, tell me and I will adjust.

This week's step is small on purpose. Ten percent of 15 running minutes is under 2 minutes, so one extra round on Saturday is the whole increase. Running pieces stay at 1 minute because I add minutes and run days before pace or longer pieces, and the longest run can only grow 2 to 3 minutes at a time.

Strides, hills and intervals stay out until you have four pain-free weeks in a row. If every week stays clean, the earliest that count reaches four is the week of Sep 28 – Oct 4. Any ache, even one that settles, restarts the count.

The goal date comes down to arithmetic. A 30-minute continuous run means at least 30 running minutes in one session, so well over 60 minutes across a week. From about 16 minutes now, a rise of about 10 percent a week takes roughly three to four months to get there, assuming every week stays pain-free.

Fitness is not what limits you, because you ran 40 km a week before the injury. The shin needs time to adapt to load, and that is why we step up slowly. Please share this plan with your physio, since they set the three run days and the stop rule.
